text:
This guide describes the health, retirement and protection benefits Mosaic Robotics offers, who is eligible for them, when elections can be made,
and how to change an election when life changes. It is written for employees of Mosaic Robotics, Inc. in the United States. Employees of Mosaic
Robotics GmbH are covered by the German statutory system supplemented by the company plans described in the *Germany Entity Supplement*
section.

Benefits are administered in MosaicOne Benefits, which is the only place an election is valid. A conversation with a manager, a message to People
Operations or a form sent to the carrier does not change an election; the election in MosaicOne does.

This guide is a summary written in plain language. The legal terms of every plan are in that plan's summary plan description, which is linked from
MosaicOne Benefits. Where this guide and a summary plan description disagree, the summary plan description governs, and People Operations will explain
the difference rather than defend the summary.

Nothing here is a promise of future benefits. Mosaic Robotics reviews its benefit offering each year and may change carriers, tiers or contribution
levels for a future plan year, with at least 60 days of notice before the change takes effect.

New hires become eligible for medical, dental and vision coverage 90 days after their hire date. Coverage begins on the day the waiting period
ends, not on the first of the following month, so an employee whose waiting period ends on 13 November is covered from 13 November.

An employee has 30 days from the end of the waiting period to make elections in MosaicOne Benefits. An employee who makes no election within that
window is enrolled in employee-only coverage on the standard medical plan by default, and may not change it until the next open enrollment or a
qualifying life event.

Retirement plan eligibility is different and shorter: an employee may begin contributing to the 401(k) plan from their first payroll run, with no
waiting period at all.

The waiting period is not restarted by an internal transfer, a promotion, or a change from part-time to full-time status. It is restarted by a
break in service of more than 26 weeks.

Employees scheduled at 0.5 FTE or more are eligible for the full benefit programme. Employees below 0.5 FTE, contractors and interns are not
eligible for company medical, dental, vision or life cover, and are eligible for the 401(k) plan only where the plan document requires it.

Dependent children may remain on a Mosaic Robotics medical plan until the end of the month in which they turn 26. Dental and vision plans follow the
same rule.

Eligible dependents are a legal spouse, a registered domestic partner, a biological or adopted child, a stepchild, and a child for whom the employee
has legal guardianship. Documentation is required within 60 days of adding a dependent; a dependent whose documentation is not supplied is removed from
coverage retroactively to the date they were added.

A child of any age who is incapable of self-support because of a disability that began before age 26 may remain covered indefinitely, subject to the
carrier's certification.

The benefits plan year runs from 1 January 2026 through 31 December 2026. Every annual maximum, deductible, contribution limit and allowance in this
guide resets on 1 January.

Elections made during open enrollment take effect on the first day of the following plan year. Elections made after a qualifying life event take
effect on the date of the event, or on the first of the following month where the carrier requires it.

Deductibles and out-of-pocket maximums do not carry over between plan years, and neither do FSA balances beyond the carryover the plan permits.
Employees who change plans mid-year through a qualifying life event should expect their deductible progress to reset with the new plan.

Open enrollment opens on 1 November 2026. Open enrollment closes on 21 November 2026 at 23:59 US Central Time.

The window is three weeks and it does not move. MosaicOne Benefits sends reminders at the opening, at the halfway point and on the final two days,
and People Operations runs two live question sessions in the second week, one at a time that works for Berlin.

An employee who makes no election during open enrollment keeps their current medical, dental and vision elections into the following plan year, at
the following year's contribution rates. Flexible spending account elections are the exception: an FSA election never rolls over and must be made again
every year, or the employee has no FSA.

Elections may be changed as often as the employee likes while the window is open. The election recorded when the window closes is the one that takes
effect.

heading_path: Open Enrollment > What You Can Change
text:
During open enrollment an employee may change medical, dental and vision plans and tiers, add or remove dependents, elect or decline life and
disability cover above the company-paid baseline, and set health and dependent-care flexible spending account contributions for the coming year.

401(k) contribution rates, investment elections and beneficiary designations are not tied to open enrollment and may be changed at any time in
MosaicOne Benefits, taking effect on the next payroll run.

Employees adding a dependent during open enrollment must supply documentation before the window closes. A dependent added without documentation is
not enrolled, and the employee finds out in January rather than in November, which is why the reminders are insistent.

Mosaic Robotics offers three medical plans for 2026: the Standard PPO, the Core HDHP with a health savings account, and the Regional HMO available
in Texas and Massachusetts only.

The Standard PPO carries an in-network individual deductible of USD 1,000 and an individual out-of-pocket maximum of USD 4,500. The Core HDHP
carries an in-network individual deductible of USD 3,300 and an individual out-of-pocket maximum of USD 6,000. The Regional HMO has no deductible for
in-network care and an individual out-of-pocket maximum of USD 3,500.

Mosaic Robotics pays 85% of the employee-only premium and 70% of the premium for each additional covered tier across all three plans. The remaining
premium is deducted from pay on a pre-tax basis over 24 semi-monthly payroll runs.

Telemedicine visits are covered at no cost on all three plans. Mental health visits are covered on the same terms as any other specialist visit,
with no separate visit limit, on all three plans.

Prescription coverage is included with every medical plan. Generic drugs carry a USD 10 copay on the PPO and the HMO, and are subject to the
deductible on the HDHP.

The dental plan covers preventive care at 100% with no deductible, basic restorative care at 80% and major restorative care at 50%, with an annual
maximum benefit of USD 2,000 per covered person. Orthodontia carries a separate lifetime maximum of USD 2,500 and is available to covered dependents
under 19.

The vision plan covers one eye examination per plan year at a USD 10 copay, and provides an allowance of USD 200 per plan year toward frames or
contact lenses. Employees whose role requires safety eyewear receive prescription safety glasses through Facilities rather than through the vision
plan, at no cost and outside the allowance.

Dental and vision elections are independent of the medical election. An employee may decline medical cover and still elect dental and vision, or the
reverse.

Mosaic Robotics matches 100% of the first 4% of eligible compensation contributed to the 401(k) plan. An employee contributing 4% or more therefore
receives the full match; an employee contributing 2% receives a 2% match.

Employer matching contributions vest after 2 years of service. Employee contributions are always immediately and fully vested, because they are the
employee's own money.

Both traditional pre-tax and Roth after-tax contributions are available, and an employee may split between them. Contribution rate changes take
effect on the next payroll run and may be made as often as the employee wishes.

New hires are automatically enrolled at a 4% pre-tax contribution rate 30 days after their start date unless they opt out or choose a different
rate. The automatic rate increases by one percentage point each January until it reaches 10%; an employee may switch the escalation off at any time.

Loans and hardship withdrawals are available under the terms of the plan document. Rollovers into the plan from a previous employer are accepted at
any time.

Mosaic Robotics contributes USD 750 per plan year to the HSA of each employee enrolled in the high-deductible medical plan. The company
contribution is paid in two instalments, in January and July, and belongs to the employee immediately.

Employees enrolled in the HDHP may make their own pre-tax HSA contributions up to the annual statutory limit, inclusive of the company
contribution. An HSA balance is the employee's property, carries over indefinitely and travels with them if they leave.

A health flexible spending account is available to employees on the PPO and HMO plans, up to the annual statutory limit. FSA balances do not carry
over indefinitely: the plan permits a carryover of up to USD 640 into the following plan year, and anything above that is forfeited.

A dependent-care flexible spending account is available to every eligible employee regardless of medical election, up to the annual statutory limit.
Dependent-care FSA balances carry over nothing at all; the funds must be used for expenses incurred within the plan year.

Mosaic Robotics provides basic life insurance and accidental death and dismemberment cover at two times base salary, up to a maximum of USD 500,000,
at no cost to the employee. Cover begins when the medical waiting period ends.

Employees may buy supplemental life cover for themselves up to a further five times base salary, and spouse and child cover at fixed amounts.
Supplemental cover elected within 30 days of first eligibility is issued without medical underwriting; elected later, it requires evidence of
insurability.

Short-term disability pays 70% of base salary for up to 13 weeks after a 7-day elimination period, at no cost to the employee. Long-term disability
pays 60% of base salary after 13 weeks, to a monthly maximum of USD 12,000, also at no cost.

Disability cover interacts with the Leave of Absence Policy. An employee on a medical leave receives disability benefit rather than salary, and
People Operations coordinates the two so there is no gap in pay.

A qualifying life event must be reported within 30 days of the event to change elections outside open enrollment. The 30 days run from the date of
the event, not from the date the employee learns the rules.

Qualifying life events are marriage, divorce or legal separation, the birth or adoption of a child, the death of a covered dependent, a change in
the employee's or a spouse's employment that changes benefit eligibility, a dependent losing or gaining other coverage, a change in residence that
changes plan availability, and a court order requiring coverage of a child.

The change made must be consistent with the event. Marriage permits adding a spouse and moving to a family tier; it does not permit switching from
the HMO to the PPO for unrelated reasons.

Documentation of the event is required within 60 days. A change made without documentation is reversed, and the employee returns to their prior
elections retroactively.

Employees of Mosaic Robotics GmbH participate in the German statutory health, pension, unemployment and long-term care systems, with contributions
split between employer and employee as the statute requires. The plans described above do not apply.

The company supplements the statutory position with a private supplementary health plan, an occupational pension contribution of 5% of gross salary
into a company-supported scheme, and a monthly public transport allowance. There is no waiting period for the supplementary plans; they begin on the
first day of employment.

German employees do not participate in open enrollment. Their supplementary elections are made at hire and may be changed at any time with one
month's notice.

Beyond the insured plans, Mosaic Robotics funds a small set of programmes aimed at the things people
actually contact People Operations about.

The employee assistance programme provides eight counselling sessions per issue per plan year, at no
cost, for the employee and every member of their household. It is confidential: the provider reports usage
volume to the company and never reports who used it or why. The programme also covers legal consultations,
financial coaching and eldercare referrals.

A family-forming benefit provides a lifetime maximum of USD 25,000 toward fertility treatment,
surrogacy, adoption costs and related travel. It is available from the first day of medical eligibility,
regardless of diagnosis, relationship status or sexual orientation.

Gender-affirming care is covered under every medical plan on the same terms as any other medically
necessary care, with a dedicated care navigator available through the carrier.

A wellbeing allowance of USD 40 per month may be claimed for exercise, sports club membership,

Three practical notes that answer most of the questions People Operations receives.

**Find your card.** Digital medical, dental and vision cards are in MosaicOne Benefits from
the day coverage begins. Physical cards arrive within fifteen days. A provider who cannot find you is
usually looking on the day before coverage started.

**Check the network first.** Every plan pays substantially more in network than out of it,
and the carrier's directory is the authority, not the provider's own website. A five-minute check before an
appointment is the single most effective thing an employee can do to control their own cost.

**Appeal a denied claim.** Carriers deny claims for administrative reasons more often than
for clinical ones, and a first-level appeal succeeds surprisingly often. People Operations will help draft
one, and will escalate on the employee's behalf where the carrier's own appeal has failed.

Employees leaving Mosaic Robotics keep medical, dental and vision cover to the end of the month in which
they leave, and are sent continuation-coverage information within fourteen days of their final day.

Benefits questions go to People Operations at benefits@mosaicrobotics.example. Eligibility and waiting-period questions, and anything involving a
dependent's documentation, go to the same address. Claims disputes with a carrier are escalated by People Operations on the employee's behalf where the
carrier's own appeal has failed. Payroll deduction questions go to payroll@mosaicrobotics.example.

This policy covers the company-owned equipment Mosaic Robotics issues to employees: laptops, monitors, docks, peripherals, mobile devices, test
instruments and the safety equipment used on the manufacturing floor. It sets what is issued as standard, how additional equipment is requested, how
assets are tracked, and what happens when something is damaged, lost or no longer needed.

Every item in this policy remains the property of Mosaic Robotics for as long as it is in service, whatever its value and wherever it sits. Items an
employee buys for themselves with the annual home office allowance described in the Expenses & Reimbursement Policy are the employee's property and are
not covered here.

All issued assets are recorded in the MosaicOne asset register against the holding employee. The register is the authoritative record of who holds
what: an item that is not in the register is not tracked, is not insured and cannot be replaced under this policy.

Equipment decisions are made by IT for computing and mobile devices, by Facilities for furniture and site equipment, and by Engineering Operations for
test instruments. People Operations owns this policy but does not own the equipment.

Every employee is issued a standard laptop configured for their role, a power adapter, a headset and a laptop bag. The standard configurations for 2026
are a 14-inch developer laptop with 32 GB of memory for engineering roles, and a 13-inch laptop with 16 GB of memory for all other roles.

Employees whose work requires more — hardware-in-the-loop simulation, large CAD assemblies, video production — are issued a high-specification laptop
or a fixed workstation on their manager's request, with no separate spending approval needed because the machines are on the standard catalogue.

Hybrid and onsite employees receive a monitor, keyboard, mouse and dock at their office desk. Fully remote employees receive the same set for their home
workspace, shipped before their start date. Hybrid employees may request a second set for home; the request is approved routinely for employees whose
recorded arrangement includes at least two remote days a week.

Mobile phones are issued only to employees in Field Service, Customer Support, Security and the executive team, and to anyone in a documented on-call
rotation. Everyone else uses their own phone and, where the role requires it, receives the connectivity stipend described in the Expenses &
Reimbursement Policy.

Manufacturing and laboratory roles are issued the personal protective equipment required for their area — safety glasses, hearing protection, ESD
footwear, cut-resistant gloves. PPE is replaced on demand and is never charged to the employee.

Company laptops are refreshed on a 36-month cycle. MosaicOne opens a refresh ticket automatically 60 days before the anniversary, and IT arranges the
swap at a time the employee chooses.

Monitors, docks and peripherals are refreshed on a 60-month cycle or on failure, whichever comes first. Mobile phones are refreshed on a 30-month
cycle. Test instruments follow the calibration and service intervals set by Engineering Operations, which are shorter and are not negotiable.

A refresh is not conditional on the old device having failed. Equipment that is still working at the end of its cycle is either redeployed to a
lower-intensity use, donated through the company's e-waste partner, or securely destroyed; the choice is IT's and is recorded against the asset.

An employee may decline a refresh and keep a working machine for up to 12 further months. After that the device leaves the supported estate, stops
receiving managed updates and must be returned, because an unpatched laptop on the network is a risk to everyone.

Additional equipment is requested through the MosaicOne equipment catalogue. Items on the catalogue have a published price, a standard configuration
and a lead time, and the request is routed for approval automatically.

Equipment requests above USD 500 require director approval in addition to manager approval. Requests at or below USD 500 need only the direct manager,
and requests for catalogue items marked *standard replacement* — a failed keyboard, a lost adapter, a worn headset — need no approval at all.

Requests for items not on the catalogue take longer, because IT reviews them for security, supportability and licence implications before Procurement
sources them. Employees should allow 15 business days for an off-catalogue request and should not buy the item themselves in the meantime: personal
purchases of computing equipment are not reimbursable.

An accommodation request — an ergonomic chair, an adjustable desk, assistive software, a specialised input device — is handled by People Operations
rather than through the catalogue, is not charged to the team's budget, and is never subject to the USD 500 threshold.

Keyboards, mice, headsets, webcams, cables, adapters and laptop stands are consumables from the company's point of view. They are issued on request
without approval, replaced on failure, and not tracked individually in the asset register below a USD 150 unit value.

Employees may choose from the catalogue's alternatives — a mechanical keyboard, a trackball, a different headset — where the alternative is within USD
75 of the standard item. Beyond that the difference needs manager approval.

External storage devices are issued only where a documented business need exists, must be hardware-encrypted, and are tracked in the asset register
regardless of value. The Security & Acceptable Use Policy's rules on removable media apply in full.

Printers are not issued for home use. Employees who need something printed use an office printer or the company's print-and-post service, because a
home printer holding company documents is a data-protection problem the company cannot see.

A lost or stolen device must be reported to IT Security within 24 hours of discovery. The report is made through the MosaicOne security incident form
or, out of hours, to the IT Security duty line printed on the back of every employee badge.

The 24-hour requirement exists so that IT Security can revoke sessions, wipe the device remotely and assess what data was resident. It is not a
disciplinary trigger and no employee has ever been penalised for reporting a loss quickly. Delaying a report, by contrast, turns a manageable incident
into a reportable data breach.

Accidental damage is covered by the company. A cracked screen, a spilled drink, a dropped instrument — these are the ordinary cost of using equipment,
and the employee is not charged. IT repairs or replaces the item and records the cause for reliability analysis.

Damage or loss resulting from clear negligence or from prohibited use may be charged to the employee at the depreciated value of the asset, with the
decision made by the VP of People Operations rather than by the employee's manager, and only where local law permits. In practice this is reserved for
repeated incidents, not for an unlucky one.

A device lost while travelling is reported on the same 24-hour clock, and the traveller also contacts the travel provider's assistance line so a
replacement can be arranged before the trip continues.

All company equipment must be returned within 5 business days of the final day of employment. IT sends a prepaid, tracked shipping label to remote
employees before their final day, and onsite employees hand equipment to their local IT desk.

The return list is generated from the asset register and shared with the employee two weeks before their final day, so that anything missing can be
found while the employee is still available to look for it. An item the employee believes was returned earlier is reconciled against the register rather
than assumed lost.

Equipment not returned within 30 calendar days of the final day is treated as unreturned company property. Mosaic Robotics may withhold the value from
the final settlement where local law permits and will otherwise pursue return through its ordinary channels.

Data on a returned device is wiped by IT under the Security & Acceptable Use Policy's media-sanitisation standard. Employees should copy any personal
files off the device before their final day, because nothing survives the wipe and IT cannot recover it afterwards.

An employee moving between Mosaic Robotics entities or between roles keeps their equipment; the asset register is updated with the new cost centre and
nothing is returned.

Software is procured by IT rather than bought on a corporate card, so that the company keeps a licence
inventory, a security review and a single renewal calendar. An employee who needs a tool raises a request
in MosaicOne naming the tool, the business need and the data it would touch.

IT answers a software request within 5 business days. The answer is one of: approved and licensed;
approved with conditions, usually about the data class it may process; already available under an existing
licence the employee did not know about, which is the most common outcome; or refused with a named
alternative.

Open-source software may be installed from the approved catalogue without a request. Anything outside the
catalogue, including a browser extension, needs the same review as a paid tool, because an extension sees
everything the browser sees.

Artificial-intelligence services are treated as any other third-party processor: approved services are
listed in MosaicOne, and company data may only be sent to those.

Personally purchased software licences are not reimbursable and are not supported. An employee who has

Licences are reclaimed when an employee changes role or leaves. IT reviews unused licences quarterly, and

Every issued asset above USD 150 is recorded in the MosaicOne asset register with its serial number, its
holder, its cost centre and its location. The register is what makes a refresh cycle, an insurance claim
and a separation return possible, and it is only as good as the data in it.

Employees can see their own asset list in MosaicOne and are asked to check it once a year during the
annual attestation. The attestation takes two minutes: confirm you hold what the register says you hold,
and flag anything that is wrong. Roughly one in twenty attestations finds a discrepancy, which is exactly
why it exists.

Facilities runs a physical audit of site equipment annually and Engineering Operations audits test
instruments quarterly, against calibration due dates rather than value. An instrument that is out of
calibration is removed from service the day it is found.

Assets transferred between employees are updated in the register at the time of transfer, by the person
handing the item over. An informal desk-to-desk handover that never reaches the register is how a laptop
ends up assigned to someone who left two years ago.

Retired assets are recorded with their disposal route — redeployed, donated through the e-waste partner,
or securely destroyed — and the certificate of destruction is retained for seven years for any device that
held Confidential or Restricted data.

Equipment requests, faults and refreshes go to IT at it-help@mosaicrobotics.example. Lost, stolen or compromised devices go to IT Security at
it-security@mosaicrobotics.example within 24 hours. Accommodation requests go to People Operations at people-ops@mosaicrobotics.example. Facilities and
site equipment questions go to facilities@mosaicrobotics.example.

This policy describes what Mosaic Robotics pays for, how an employee claims it back, and who approves it. It covers business expenses incurred by
employees of Mosaic Robotics, Inc. and Mosaic Robotics GmbH in the ordinary course of their work, together with the standing allowances the company
offers for home offices, connectivity and professional development.

Travel expenses — flights, hotels, ground transport, per diem — are set out in the Travel Policy, which sits alongside this one and shares its
submission mechanics, deadlines and approval thresholds. Where the Travel Policy sets a cap, that cap governs; where it is silent, this policy governs.

All expenses are submitted in MosaicOne Expenses. Reimbursement is paid with the next payroll run after approval, which means an expense approved by
the 20th of a month is reimbursed in that month's payroll and an expense approved after it lands in the following month.

Amounts in this policy are stated in United States dollars. Employees of the German entity claim in euros; MosaicOne converts the cap at the European
Central Bank reference rate on the transaction date, and the converted figure — not a re-negotiated one — is the cap that applies.

Four principles decide every case this policy does not name explicitly.

**Business purpose.** An expense is reimbursable when it was incurred to do Mosaic Robotics work and would not have been incurred otherwise. A meal
eaten while travelling for the company is reimbursable; the same meal eaten at home is not.

**Reasonableness.** Spend company money as you would spend your own, on a day when you were paying attention. The caps below are ceilings, not targets,
and nobody has ever been criticised for coming in under one.

**Transparency.** The claim should describe what was bought, for whom, and why, in language a colleague outside the team would understand. "Client
dinner" is not a description; "Dinner with three engineers from Northwind Automation after the on-site integration test" is.

**No self-approval.** Nobody approves their own expense report, and nobody approves the expense report of a person who approves theirs. Reports from
executives are approved by the CFO; the CFO's are approved by the CEO.

Where an employee is unsure whether something is reimbursable, the answer is to ask before spending. People Operations and Finance would far rather
answer a question than refuse a claim.

Expenses must be submitted within 45 calendar days of the transaction date. The transaction date is the date on the receipt, not the date the card
statement posted and not the date the trip ended.

A claim submitted after the deadline is not automatically refused, but it requires director approval with a written reason, and MosaicOne flags it as
late. Finance reports the volume of late claims to department heads quarterly, because a persistent pattern usually means a broken process rather than
a careless person.

Claims relating to a plan year must be submitted by 15 January of the following year without exception. The company closes its books on 31 January and
cannot reopen a prior year for an individual claim.

Each claim line carries the transaction date, the amount, the currency, the merchant, the business purpose and — where applicable — the names of the
other attendees. MosaicOne pre-fills most of this from the corporate card feed; the business purpose is always the employee's to write.

An itemised receipt is required for every expense of USD 25 or more. *Itemised* means the receipt shows what was bought, not only the total: a
restaurant's card slip is not sufficient on its own where the itemised bill is available.

Expenses under USD 25 may be claimed without a receipt where the corporate card feed shows the merchant and amount. Cash expenses of any value require
a receipt, because there is no card record to corroborate them.

A lost receipt is handled with a missing-receipt declaration in MosaicOne: the employee states what was bought and why, and the manager approves the
declaration alongside the claim. More than three missing-receipt declarations in a plan year triggers a conversation with Finance.

Receipts must be legible and complete. A photograph of a receipt is fine; a photograph of half a receipt, or of a screen showing a booking confirmation
without a price, is not. MosaicOne stores receipt images for seven years to satisfy audit requirements.

heading_path: Home Office and Equipment Stipends > Annual Home Office Allowance
text:
Each employee may claim up to USD 750 per plan year for home office furniture and accessories. The allowance is intended for the things that make a
home workspace work: a desk, a chair, a lamp, a footrest, an adjustable monitor arm, acoustic treatment, a small filing cabinet.

The allowance resets on 1 January and does not carry over. It is available to hybrid and fully remote employees; onsite employees may claim against it
only where their manager has agreed a regular remote pattern in MosaicOne.

Laptops, monitors, docks, keyboards, mice, headsets and webcams are **not** claimed against this allowance. They are issued as company assets under the
Equipment & Asset Policy, remain company property and are tracked in the asset register. An employee who buys a monitor with the home office allowance
has bought a monitor for themselves, which is rarely what they intended.

Items purchased under the allowance belong to the employee and are not returned at separation. Because of that, the allowance is taxable in some
jurisdictions; MosaicOne applies the correct treatment automatically for each entity.

A new hire may claim the full allowance from their start date. An employee who joins after 1 October may claim the following year's allowance
immediately as well, so that a December start is not penalised.

heading_path: Home Office and Equipment Stipends > Monthly Connectivity Stipend
text:
Fully remote employees receive a monthly connectivity stipend of USD 60. The stipend is paid automatically through payroll, requires no claim and no
receipt, and is intended to cover the incremental cost of home internet and mobile data used for work.

Hybrid and onsite employees do not receive the connectivity stipend, because the company provides connectivity at the office. A hybrid employee whose
role requires reliable home connectivity for on-call duty may request the stipend through their manager, and it is granted for the duration of the
on-call assignment.

The stipend is not paid for months in which the employee is on unpaid leave. It continues during paid leave, PTO and approved work abroad.

The daily meal cap for domestic travel is USD 75 per traveller. The cap covers all meals in a 24-hour period including tips and non-alcoholic drinks,
and it applies per person rather than per receipt, so a shared dinner for three colleagues is measured against USD 225.

Alcohol is reimbursable only as part of a hosted meal with customers, partners or candidates, and only in moderation. Alcohol claimed on a solo travel
day is refused.

Team meals — a lunch for a team that has just shipped, a dinner during an offsite — are reimbursable with manager approval. The claim names every
attendee. A team meal of more than USD 100 per head requires director approval.

Meals with candidates are reimbursable by the hiring manager under the same caps. Meals with a supplier, or any hospitality offered by a supplier to a
Mosaic Robotics employee, must also be checked against the conflict-of-interest rules in the Workplace Conduct Policy.

Each employee has a professional development budget of USD 1,500 per plan year. It covers conference registration, training courses, professional
certification fees, technical books and paid subscriptions to learning platforms.

The budget resets on 1 January and does not carry over. Travel to a conference is claimed against the Travel Policy, not against the professional
development budget, so the USD 1,500 buys learning rather than flights.

Spending the budget requires manager approval in advance, recorded in MosaicOne, because a manager should know what their team is learning. Approval is
routine; the record is the point.

Professional membership dues are reimbursable where membership is relevant to the employee's role. Certification fees are reimbursable including one
re-sit; a second re-sit is at the employee's expense.

An employee who leaves Mosaic Robotics within 90 days of a reimbursed training course costing more than USD 1,000 repays the cost on a pro-rata basis,
where local law permits and where the repayment obligation was agreed in writing before the course.

The following are never reimbursed: parking and traffic fines, personal grooming, in-flight entertainment and connectivity on flights under three
hours, personal travel insurance beyond the company policy, childcare and pet care, home internet for hybrid employees, personal phone handsets,
political and charitable donations, gym memberships, and expenses incurred by a family member accompanying an employee on business travel.

Software and cloud services are not reimbursable as personal expenses. They are procured by IT so that the company keeps a licence inventory and a
security review; an employee who needs a tool raises a request with IT rather than buying it on a corporate card.

Gifts to customers or partners above USD 100 per recipient per year require director approval and a check against the anti-bribery language in the
Workplace Conduct Policy. Gifts to public officials of any value are prohibited.

Expenses that appear on an employee's corporate card but are personal must be repaid within 30 calendar days. Repeated personal use of a corporate card
results in the card being withdrawn.

This policy sets out which matters must be escalated to a named human being in People Operations, how a case is raised, how quickly it is answered, and
how it is kept confidential. It applies to employees of Mosaic Robotics, Inc. and Mosaic Robotics GmbH, and to anyone acting on the company's behalf who
becomes aware of a matter within its scope.

It exists because Mosaic Robotics runs self-service tools — MosaicOne, its policy search, and an HR assistant that answers policy questions — and those
tools must have a clearly drawn boundary. Some questions are looked up. Others are handled by a person, with judgement, discretion and a case record.
This document draws that boundary.

Nothing here replaces the Workplace Conduct Policy, which defines prohibited conduct and describes the investigation process. This policy is about
routing and response: who hears about a matter, how fast, and what the person raising it can expect.

Managers are subject to an additional duty. A manager who learns of a matter listed in the next section must route it to People Operations the same
working day, whether or not the affected person asked them to and whether or not they think it serious.

Harassment, discrimination, legal threats, medical conditions and compensation disputes are never handled by an automated assistant and are routed to a
named People Operations partner. The assistant's correct response to any of them is to say so, to name the route, and to stop.

A case may be raised in MosaicOne under *Raise an HR case*, by email to the addresses in the *Contacts* section, in person to any member of People
Operations, or anonymously through the third-party ethics line published in MosaicOne.

The HR assistant can open a case on an employee's behalf, but only after the employee has explicitly confirmed the summary it proposes. It never opens a
case silently, never opens one from an inferred intent, and never fills in details the employee did not give it. Every case it opens is marked with its
origin so the People Operations partner knows how the summary was produced.

A case needs, at minimum, the name of the person raising it and a description of the matter. Dates, names of others involved and any documents are
helpful and are not required. A person who is not ready to give details may open a case saying only that they want to speak to someone.

Where a person asks for confidentiality before describing a matter, People Operations explains honestly what it can and cannot promise: it will share
information only with those who need it to act, and it cannot promise to take no action at all where the matter involves a risk to another person.

Every case receives a case reference on creation. The reference is the way to ask about progress, and it appears on every message the company sends
about the case.

Every case is assigned a severity on creation by the People Operations partner who receives it. Severity drives response time, not outcome, and it can
be raised at any point as more is learned.

**Severity 1** covers immediate risk to a person: violence or a threat of it, a safety incident with injury, a credible risk of self-harm, sexual
misconduct involving physical contact, and any matter where someone must be separated from a situation today. Severity 1 cases receive a response within
4 business hours.

**Severity 2** covers serious matters without immediate physical risk: harassment, discrimination, retaliation, suspected fraud, a regulatory inquiry, a
legal threat. Severity 2 cases receive a first response within 1 business day and a written plan within 3 business days.

**Severity 3** covers everything else that requires a person: accommodation requests, compensation disputes, undisclosed conflicts of interest, and
matters an employee has asked to be handled formally. Severity 3 cases receive a response within 3 business days.

Response means a named human being contacting the person who raised the case, acknowledging what was raised, naming who owns it and describing what
happens next. It does not mean an outcome, and People Operations is careful not to imply otherwise.

Target resolution times are 10 business days for Severity 3, 30 calendar days for Severity 2 and as fast as the facts allow for Severity 1. Where a case
will run past its target, the person who raised it is told in writing why and when to expect the next update. Updates continue at least every 10
business days until the case closes.

Case records are held in a restricted store separate from the ordinary employee file. Access is limited to the People Operations partners handling the
case, the VP of People Operations, and where necessary external counsel. A manager is not given access to a case record about their own team.

Information is shared on a need-to-know basis and no wider. A respondent is told the substance of an allegation because a fair process requires it; they
are not told who else was interviewed or what any witness said beyond what is necessary to respond.

Medical information supplied in support of a leave, an accommodation or a disability claim is held separately again, is never shared with a manager, and
is described to a manager only as a schedule or a set of adjustments.

Case records are retained for six years after closure and are then destroyed, except where a legal hold applies. Aggregate case statistics — volume,
category, resolution time — are reported to the executive team and the board quarterly, with no identifying detail.

Anyone who discloses case information outside the need-to-know boundary, including a person who raised a case discussing another party's response, is
subject to the Workplace Conduct Policy. Confidentiality protects the process for everyone in it.

The HR assistant answers policy questions from this corpus, looks up an employee's own structured data, and can draft messages and open mock tickets
when the employee confirms. It is a convenience layer over the same policies a person would otherwise read.

Three rules bound it. It never answers a matter on the escalation list, and instead names the route and the contact. It never performs an action that
creates a record without an explicit confirmation from the person, shown to them with the exact details first. And it never invents policy: an answer
that is not supported by a citation into this corpus is not given.

An employee may always bypass the assistant and contact People Operations directly. Nobody is required to interact with a tool to reach a person, and
People Operations does not ask whether the assistant was tried first.

Conversations with the assistant are logged for audit and quality purposes, are subject to the same confidentiality rules as any other HR record, and
are retained under the same schedule.

Most concerns reach People Operations through a manager, which makes the manager's first response the most
important part of this whole process.

A manager who is told something within the escalation list does four things. Listen without judging the
account. Say plainly that they are required to pass it to People Operations, and why, rather than promising
a confidentiality they cannot deliver. Ask what the person needs right now, which is often something simple
like not being scheduled on the same shift this week. And route it the same working day.

A manager does not investigate. They do not interview the other party, do not gather statements, do not
warn anyone, and do not test the account against their own knowledge. Every one of those actions, however
well meant, damages an investigation that has not started yet and can make the company's position worse
than if nothing had been done at all.

A manager who is themselves the subject of a concern is told by People Operations, not by the reporter, and
is given a fair opportunity to respond.

The manager fundamentals training covers this section directly, with practice conversations, because
knowing the rule and being able to say it out loud at the moment somebody starts crying are different

People Operations reports four numbers to the executive team and the board each quarter: case volume by
category, median time to first response against the severity target, median time to closure, and the share
of cases reopened within 90 days.

No individual is identifiable in the reporting. Categories with fewer than five cases in a quarter are
aggregated so that a small team's single case cannot be inferred from the numbers.

Reporters and witnesses are surveyed after closure on whether they were treated fairly and whether they
would raise a concern again. The second question is the one the company watches most closely, because a
process that resolves cases while teaching people not to report has failed.

Trends are acted on rather than filed. Three cases from the same team in a quarter, a category rising
without an obvious cause, or a persistent gap between severity targets and actual response times each
trigger a review with the department head involved.

The escalation list itself is reviewed annually against the cases that arrived, and categories are added
when the year's experience shows a gap. It has grown twice since 2024 and has never shrunk.

employee-relations@mosaicrobotics.example. Leave and accommodation matters go to leave@mosaicrobotics.example. Safety incidents go to
safety@mosaicrobotics.example and, where anyone is hurt, to the site emergency number first. Security incidents go to
it-security@mosaicrobotics.example. Reports concerning the executive team go to the third-party ethics line published in MosaicOne, which routes them to
the chair of the audit committee.

This policy describes the extended absences Mosaic Robotics supports: parental leave, medical leave, family care leave, bereavement, civic duty and
unpaid personal leave. It applies to employees of Mosaic Robotics, Inc. and, with the differences noted in the *Germany Entity Differences* section, to
employees of Mosaic Robotics GmbH.

A leave of absence is different from PTO in three ways that matter. It is longer, it is protected — the employee's job and benefits continue on defined
terms — and it is administered by People Operations rather than by the employee's manager. Nothing in this policy consumes PTO, and an employee does
not need to exhaust PTO before taking a leave.

Where a statutory entitlement exists that is more generous than the company benefit described here, the statutory entitlement applies and the company
benefit is layered on top rather than substituted for it. People Operations administers the interaction; the employee does not need to work it out.

Every leave is recorded in MosaicOne with a start date, an expected return date, the type of leave and the pay treatment. Managers see the dates and the
type. Managers do not see medical information, and People Operations does not share it with them.

Mosaic Robotics provides 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave to every eligible new parent. The 16 weeks are the same whether the employee gave birth,
did not give birth, adopted, or became a parent through surrogacy or foster placement leading to adoption.

Parental leave eligibility begins after 6 months of continuous service. An employee who becomes a parent before reaching six months receives the
statutory entitlement their jurisdiction provides, and the company benefit begins the day the service requirement is met.

Leave must begin within 12 months of the birth or placement. It may be taken as one continuous block, or as up to three blocks of at least two weeks
each, agreed with the manager and People Operations before the first block begins. Splitting the leave does not extend the total.

An employee who gives birth also receives any period of medical disability leave certified by their clinician, before the parental leave begins. The
disability period is paid through short-term disability rather than as parental leave, and it does not reduce the 16 weeks.

Parental leave for both parents where both work at Mosaic Robotics is 16 weeks each. The company does not pool or reduce the entitlement.

Continuous medical leave is available for up to 26 weeks in a rolling 12-month period. The leave covers the employee's own serious health condition,
including physical illness, surgery, recovery and mental health treatment.

The first 13 weeks are paid at 70% of base salary through short-term disability after a 7-day elimination period covered by the employee's sick balance
or PTO. Weeks 14 to 26 are paid at 60% of base salary through long-term disability. Mosaic Robotics tops the first two weeks up to 100% of base salary
so that a short recovery is not a financial event.

Intermittent medical leave — a course of treatment requiring a day a week, a reduced schedule during recovery — is available on the same 26-week
budget, counted in hours rather than weeks. The schedule is agreed with People Operations and the manager is told only the schedule.

A clinician's certification is required for any medical leave longer than five consecutive working days, and a recertification is required every eight
weeks for a continuing leave. Certifications go to People Operations and are stored in a restricted-access record separate from the employee file.

heading_path: Types of Leave > Family Care Leave
text:
Family care leave provides up to 12 weeks in a rolling 12-month period to care for a spouse, registered domestic partner, child, parent, parent-in-law
or sibling with a serious health condition, or for a family member's military deployment.

The first 4 weeks are paid at 100% of base salary. The remaining 8 weeks are unpaid, and the employee may use PTO to cover part or all of them if they
choose. Benefits continue in full for the whole 12 weeks.

Family care leave may be taken continuously or intermittently, and the 12 weeks are separate from the 26 weeks of medical leave. An employee who needs
both in the same year receives both.

Bereavement leave provides 5 paid days for the death of an immediate family member. Immediate family means a spouse or partner, a child, a parent, a
sibling, a grandparent, a grandchild, and the equivalent in-law relationships.

Three paid days are provided for the death of any other person with whom the employee had a close relationship, at the employee's own description; the
company does not adjudicate the relationship.

Bereavement leave is taken within 60 days of the death and need not be consecutive, so that an employee can attend a service that happens weeks later.
Additional time is available as PTO or as unpaid personal leave, and People Operations will arrange it without requiring the employee to negotiate.

Pregnancy loss is bereavement leave, at 5 paid days, for both parents.

heading_path: Types of Leave > Jury Duty and Civic Leave
text:
Jury service is paid at full salary for up to 10 days per plan year. Longer service is paid at full salary where the employee assigns the court's
stipend to the company, and People Operations arranges this with payroll.

Time spent responding to a subpoena in a matter connected to the employee's Mosaic Robotics work is paid working time and is not counted against civic
leave.

Voting leave is provided as the law of the employee's jurisdiction requires, and in every case Mosaic Robotics provides at least two paid hours to vote
where the polls are not open outside the employee's working hours.

Volunteer emergency service — a volunteer firefighter, a search-and-rescue team member, a reserve responder — is supported with up to 5 paid days per
plan year for call-outs and required training.

heading_path: Types of Leave > Unpaid Personal Leave
text:
Unpaid personal leave of up to 12 weeks may be requested for a reason not covered elsewhere in this policy: study, an extended family commitment, a
personal project. It is granted at the discretion of the department head with People Operations' agreement, and it is not an entitlement.

Benefits continue during unpaid personal leave, with the employee paying their ordinary share of the premium by direct payment to payroll. PTO does not
accrue during unpaid leave and the connectivity stipend is not paid.

An employee on unpaid personal leave keeps their role for the agreed period. A leave longer than 12 weeks is possible only where the department head
and the VP of People Operations agree in advance that the role can be held open.

Foreseeable leave must be requested at least 30 calendar days in advance. The request is raised in MosaicOne under *Request a leave of absence* and
names the type of leave, the intended start date and the expected duration.

Unforeseeable leave — an accident, a sudden diagnosis, a death — is requested as soon as the employee reasonably can, by any means, to their manager or
directly to People Operations. Nothing in this policy requires a sick person to file a form before they receive care.

People Operations responds to every leave request within 3 business days with a written summary: the type of leave approved, the pay treatment, the
benefits treatment, what certification is needed and by when, and who the employee's named contact will be for the duration.

The manager's role is to plan coverage, not to approve the leave. A statutory or company leave entitlement is not a request a manager can refuse, and
People Operations will tell a manager so plainly if it comes up.

An employee may extend a leave by contacting People Operations before the expected return date. An extension within the entitlement is administrative;
an extension beyond it is considered as unpaid personal leave.

Medical, dental, vision, life and disability cover continue unchanged during every paid leave in this policy, with the employee's share of the premium
deducted from any pay they receive and invoiced where pay is insufficient.

During unpaid leave the employee remains enrolled and pays their ordinary share by direct payment to payroll. Missing three consecutive payments ends
cover, and People Operations gives 30 days of written warning before that happens.

PTO accrues normally during paid leave. It does not accrue during unpaid leave, and it does not accrue during any period in which the employee is
receiving long-term disability benefit.

401(k) contributions continue from any pay the employee receives, and the company match continues on the same terms. Contributions stop during unpaid
periods and resume automatically on return, at the same rate.

Service for the purpose of tenure, PTO accrual bands and vesting continues to accumulate during every protected leave, paid or unpaid.

An employee returning from leave returns to the same role, at the same level and the same base pay. Where the role no longer exists because of an
organisational change that would have affected the employee regardless of the leave, they return to an equivalent role, and People Operations reviews
the change before it is made.

A return from medical leave requires a clinician's fitness-to-return statement, which says only whether the employee is fit and what accommodations if
any are needed. It contains no diagnosis and is held by People Operations.

Where a phased return is recommended — reduced hours for a period, a temporary change of duties — People Operations arranges it with the manager. A
phased return is normal after a long absence and is not a performance signal.

An employee who cannot return at the end of their entitlement is supported through a reasonable-accommodation review before any other conversation
happens. Termination at the end of a leave is a last resort, requires VP of People Operations approval, and never happens without that review.

German employees receive statutory Mutterschutz, Elternzeit and Pflegezeit entitlements, which are more extensive than the company parental and family
care benefits described above. The company benefit tops up statutory pay to 100% of net salary for the first 16 weeks of Elternzeit.

Medical absence in Germany is covered by statutory Entgeltfortzahlung for the first six weeks at full pay, followed by Krankengeld from the statutory
health insurer. The company's short-term disability plan does not apply; the company tops up Krankengeld to 90% of net salary for up to 26 weeks.

German statutory vacation entitlement interacts with the PTO carryover rules in the PTO & Holidays Policy. Where the statute requires a longer carryover
window, the statute applies.

All other sections of this policy — request mechanics, benefits continuation, return to work, confidentiality — apply to German employees unchanged.

Mosaic Robotics offers a paid sabbatical of 4 consecutive weeks to every employee who reaches 5 years of
continuous service, and again at each subsequent five-year anniversary. The sabbatical is in addition to
PTO and does not draw down any balance.

Eligibility is checked automatically in MosaicOne on the service anniversary, and the employee is
notified. The sabbatical must be taken within 24 months of the anniversary or it lapses; it cannot be
banked, deferred indefinitely, or exchanged for pay.

A sabbatical is requested at least 90 calendar days in advance so that coverage can be planned properly.
The manager and the department head agree the dates; the entitlement itself is not discretionary and is
never refused, only scheduled.

The point of a sabbatical is a genuine break, so an employee on sabbatical is removed from on-call
rotations, from meeting invitations and from routine distribution lists, and their accounts stay active
only so that nothing breaks on their return. Colleagues are asked not to contact them about work, and

heading_path: Escalation When an Approver Is Unavailable
text:
If an approver does not respond within 3 business days, the request escalates automatically to the skip-level manager. The original approver keeps
visibility of the request and can still act on it until the skip-level manager decides.

An approver who will be unavailable for more than three business days delegates their approval authority in MosaicOne before they go. Delegation is to a
named person at the same level or above, is time-bounded, and is visible on every request it touches.

Escalation moves a decision; it does not make one. A skip-level manager who receives an escalated request may approve it, refuse it, or hold it until
the original approver returns, and is expected to say which.

Requests that are urgent and cannot wait three business days are marked urgent by the requester with a one-line reason, which shortens the escalation
window to one business day. Urgency is self-declared and is reviewed by People Operations quarterly; a person who marks everything urgent is asked to
stop.

Where an approval is required by law or by a statutory entitlement — a leave of absence, a reasonable accommodation, a statutory notice period — no
escalation timer applies, because the request is not a matter of managerial discretion in the first place.

An approver who will be unavailable for more than three business days delegates their authority in
MosaicOne before they go. Delegation is set up in under a minute and prevents every downstream problem in
this section.

A delegation names one person, at the same level or above, and a start and end date. It cannot be open
ended, cannot be to a direct report, and cannot be chained: a delegate may not re-delegate to a third
person. Every request touched by a delegation shows both names on the record.

A delegate carries the delegating approver's authority in full, including any spending limit, but not their
own limit in addition. A director delegating to another director does not create a doubled threshold.

Where an approver has left the company, MosaicOne routes their pending requests to the skip-level manager
automatically on the final day, and People Operations reassigns the reporting lines within one business
day so that future requests route correctly.
