the supplier's own breach notification commitment is. Confidential and Restricted data may only be
processed by suppliers who have passed that review and signed the company's data processing agreement.

Customer data that reaches Mosaic Robotics as part of a field service or integration engagement is treated
as Confidential at minimum, is held only for as long as the engagement needs it, and is returned or
destroyed at its end with a written confirmation to the customer.

Suppliers do not connect their own devices to Mosaic Robotics production networks. A guest network is
provided for visitors, and any device that must reach a production system is provided and managed by IT.

Security and acceptable-use training is completed within 14 calendar days of the start date and refreshed
annually, as the Onboarding and First 90 Days document sets out. The refresh is short, is different every
year, and is not a re-run of the same slides.

IT Security runs simulated phishing exercises quarterly against the whole company. A person who clicks a
simulation receives a short, private explanation of what the signals were; nobody is named to their manager
and nobody is disciplined for a simulation. The company measures the aggregate click rate and the aggregate
report rate, and cares far more about the second number than the first.

Role-specific training is provided where the risk warrants it: secure development for engineers, data
handling for People Operations and Finance, and customer-site security for Field Service.

A short monthly note goes to the whole company describing one real thing that happened, in the industry or
at Mosaic Robotics, with the identifying details removed. Concrete stories change behaviour and abstract
warnings do not.

Employees who want to understand a control rather than just comply with it can ask IT Security for the
reasoning, and will get it. A control nobody understands is a control everybody works around.

Security incidents, suspected compromises and lost devices go to it-security@mosaicrobotics.example or to the
duty line on the back of the employee badge. Suspected phishing goes to phishing@mosaicrobotics.example.
Requests for software approval, access changes and encrypted removable media go to it-help@mosaicrobotics.example.
Questions about how this policy applies to a particular situation go to it-security@mosaicrobotics.example,
and questions about the consequences of breaching it go to people-ops@mosaicrobotics.example.

This addendum sits underneath the Remote & Hybrid Work Policy and governs the consequences of *where* work is physically performed. The Remote & Hybrid
Work Policy answers whether an arrangement suits the role and the team. This addendum answers whether the company and the employee can lawfully and
affordably carry it.

It applies to every employee of Mosaic Robotics, Inc. and Mosaic Robotics GmbH who intends to perform work from a country other than the one their
employment contract is registered in, and to every permanent relocation across a national border. It also applies to Mosaic Robotics itself: the
thresholds below are the company's obligations as much as the employee's.

Nothing in this addendum is personal tax advice. Mosaic Robotics can describe its own obligations and can tell an employee what the company will and
will not do. It cannot tell an employee what their personal tax return should say, and it does not reimburse personal tax preparation except where the
*Payroll and Withholding* section says so explicitly.

Where this addendum and the Remote & Hybrid Work Policy both set a requirement, both apply. Where they appear to conflict, the stricter requirement
governs and People Operations resolves the conflict in writing.

Three separate legal systems attach to the physical location of work, and they do not share a single threshold.

**Immigration** asks whether the person has the right to be present and to work. It is binary and it is the destination country's decision. A tourist
entry that permits remote work for a foreign employer in one country is a criminal matter in another, and neither Mosaic Robotics nor the employee can
negotiate it.

**Payroll and personal tax** ask which authority is owed withholding on the employee's earnings, and from which day. Some countries begin at the first
day of presence, most apply a treaty-based day count, and a few look at where the economic employer sits rather than where the person is.

**Corporate tax** asks whether the employee's activity creates a taxable presence — a *permanent establishment* — for Mosaic Robotics in the destination
country. This is the risk with the largest financial consequence and the one an employee is least likely to have considered, because it depends on what
the employee *does* rather than on how long they stay.

The thresholds in this addendum are set conservatively against all three, which is why they are shorter than the day counts an employee may find in a
tax treaty.

heading_path: Duration Thresholds > Stays Up To 30 Days
text:
A stay of 30 consecutive days or fewer in an approved country requires manager approval under the Remote & Hybrid Work Policy and nothing further from
Tax & Legal. The employee remains on their home payroll, no shadow withholding is set up, and no corporate-tax filing is triggered.

The employee must still hold the right to work in the destination country, must still meet the device and connectivity requirements, and must still
stay inside the company's rolling 90-day annual limit. A short stay is administratively simple; it is not unregulated.

Consecutive days are counted from the first calendar day of presence to the last, inclusive of weekends and holidays. Two trips separated by fewer than
14 days are treated as one continuous stay for the purposes of this threshold, so an employee cannot reset the count with a weekend flight home.

A stay of more than 30 consecutive days in another country requires a Tax & Legal review before travel begins. The review determines whether shadow
payroll must be opened, whether a certificate of coverage is needed for social security, and whether the employee's planned activities create
permanent-establishment exposure.

Tax & Legal review requests must be filed at least 21 calendar days before departure. The request is raised in MosaicOne alongside the manager approval
and names the destination, the exact dates, the workspace address and a short description of the work the employee will perform while abroad.

A review has one of three outcomes. **Approved** — the trip proceeds as requested. **Approved with conditions** — the trip proceeds with named
restrictions, most often a prohibition on customer-facing activity and a hard end date. **Not approved** — the exposure cannot be managed at a
reasonable cost, and the employee is offered an alternative destination or a shorter stay.

A trip that exceeds 30 consecutive days also requires director approval rather than direct-manager approval, as set out in the Manager Approval Matrix.
Manager approval, director approval and Tax & Legal approval are three separate records and all three must be present before departure.

A permanent relocation to another country requires 60 calendar days of notice and a new employment agreement. A relocation is not an extended trip: the
employee's contract, payroll, benefits, holiday calendar and often their job title change, and the change is only possible into a country where Mosaic
Robotics already has an entity.

Mosaic Robotics has entities in the United States and Germany. A relocation to any other country is not available and is refused regardless of tenure,
performance or business case; the alternative offered is a temporary stay inside the 90-day limit.

An approved relocation terminates the employee's participation in the origin country's benefit plans on the transfer date and enrols them in the
destination country's plans, subject to that plan's waiting period. Accrued PTO transfers at its recorded value where the law permits, and is otherwise
paid out.

Relocation support — shipping, temporary housing, immigration counsel — is approved case by case by the VP of People Operations and is documented in
the relocation agreement, not in this addendum.

Germany, Ireland, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain, Canada and Mexico are approved destinations for temporary work abroad. The list is maintained by
Tax & Legal and reviewed twice a year; it reflects where the company has an entity, a treaty position it understands, or a low enough exposure to
accept.

A destination not on the list is not automatically refused, but it requires a Tax & Legal assessment that typically takes 30 calendar days rather than
21, and it is more often refused than approved. Employees planning an unlisted destination should raise it early rather than after booking travel.

Work from a country subject to United States or European Union sanctions, or from a country on the company's elevated-risk list maintained by IT
Security, is prohibited outright and no exception process exists.

Approval of a country is not approval of a trip. Every trip needs its own manager approval, and every trip over 30 consecutive days needs its own Tax &
Legal review, regardless of how many colleagues have worked from the same country before.

An employee working abroad remains on their home payroll unless Tax & Legal open a shadow payroll. Shadow payroll reports the same earnings to a second
authority so that withholding can be remitted where it is owed; it does not change the employee's net pay, though it usually changes the timing of
their personal filings.

Presence of more than 183 days in a calendar year in a single foreign country generally creates personal tax residency there. The 183-day figure is a
common treaty threshold and not a promise: several countries apply shorter tests, and the company's own 90-day limit is set well below it precisely so
that no employee stumbles across the line by accident.

Where a company-directed assignment causes an employee to owe tax in two countries on the same earnings, Mosaic Robotics funds tax-equalisation support
through its external provider. Where an employee-requested trip does the same, the employee is responsible for their own filings and the company will
supply the payroll records needed to complete them.

Social security is handled separately from income tax. For stays in countries with a totalisation agreement, Tax & Legal obtain a certificate of
coverage so that contributions continue in the home system; without one, the employee and the company may both owe contributions twice.

A permanent establishment is a taxable presence that a company creates in a country by having a fixed place of business there, or by having a person
there who habitually concludes contracts on its behalf. Creating one exposes Mosaic Robotics to corporate tax, filing obligations and penalties in that
country for years afterwards.

Employees working abroad may not sign contracts or negotiate customer agreements on behalf of Mosaic Robotics while outside their home country. This is
the single most important restriction in this addendum. It applies to every employee on every approved trip, including trips under 30 days, and it
applies regardless of the employee's job title.

Related restrictions apply to the same risk. An employee abroad may not hold themselves out as a Mosaic Robotics representative in the destination
country, may not use a destination-country address on company materials, and may not rent premises in the company's name.

Engineering, support and internal work carry very little permanent-establishment risk. Sales, business development, partnerships and executive roles
carry a great deal. Tax & Legal weight their review accordingly, and an employee in a commercial role should expect a more restrictive answer than a
colleague in engineering asking for the same trip.

The employee is responsible for holding the right to be present and to work in the destination country for the whole of the requested period. Mosaic
Robotics will confirm employment, provide a letter of assignment and pay for the assignment letter's notarisation where required, and will not sponsor
a visa for temporary work abroad.

An employee who is refused entry, whose permission expires mid-trip, or who is told by an immigration officer that their activity is not permitted must
stop working immediately and contact mobility@mosaicrobotics.example. Continuing to work in that situation puts both the employee and the company at
risk and is treated as a serious matter.

Non-citizens working in the United States on a company-sponsored visa should assume that any period abroad has immigration consequences at home, and
must speak to People Operations before requesting a trip of any length. The rules governing re-entry are stricter than the rules governing departure.

**"I am visiting family in Germany for three weeks and would like to work rather than take PTO."** That is
a stay of 21 consecutive days in an approved country. Manager approval under the Remote & Hybrid Work
Policy is enough, requested at least 21 calendar days ahead, and no Tax & Legal review is required. The
device requirements apply in full and the days count against the rolling 90-day annual limit.

**"The same trip, but six weeks."** That is 42 days, over the 30-day threshold, so it needs director

usually approve it with conditions: a hard end date and a prohibition on customer-facing activity.

**"I want to move to Portugal permanently."** Mosaic Robotics has no Portuguese entity, so a permanent
relocation there is not available. The alternative is a stay inside the 90-day annual limit, or a
conversation about whether the role could be based in Berlin.

**"I am attending a conference in Japan for four days."** That is business travel under the Travel Policy,

**"I did not ask and I have been working from Spain for two months."** Tell mobility@mosaicrobotics.example
today. Unwinding an exposure that is disclosed is administrative; discovering one in an audit two years
later is expensive, and the difference in how the company responds is entirely about the disclosure.

Tax and legal questions about working abroad go to tax-legal@mosaicrobotics.example. Mobility logistics, approvals and destination questions go to
mobility@mosaicrobotics.example. Device, network and travel-risk questions go to it-security@mosaicrobotics.example. General questions about work

This policy covers business travel by employees of Mosaic Robotics, Inc. and Mosaic Robotics GmbH: customer visits, field service calls, supplier
audits, conferences, inter-office visits and team offsites. It sets what may be booked, through which channel, at what cost, and with whose approval.

Business travel is travel undertaken at the company's request or with the company's approval to perform work at a location other than the employee's
normal place of work. It is not the same thing as working from another country, which is governed by the Remote & Hybrid Work Policy and the Tax &
Location Addendum; a trip that begins as travel and turns into a period of remote work needs approvals under both documents.

Submission mechanics, receipt rules and approval thresholds are shared with the Expenses & Reimbursement Policy. This document sets only the additional
caps and rules that travel needs.

Mosaic Robotics ships heavy, calibrated hardware and sends engineers to install it. Field travel is therefore a core operating cost rather than an
occasional perk, and this policy is written to keep it predictable rather than to discourage it.

All travel is booked through MosaicOne Travel, which is connected to the company's travel management provider. Booking through the tool is what puts
the traveller on the company's duty-of-care roster, so a trip booked outside it is invisible to the company in an emergency and is reimbursed only with
director approval.

Flights must be booked at least 14 calendar days before departure whenever the itinerary is known. Advance purchase is the single largest lever on
travel cost, and the 14-day rule typically halves a domestic fare.

Travel that cannot be booked 14 days ahead — an emergency field call, a customer escalation, a supplier failure — is booked as soon as the need is
known and does not require an exception. MosaicOne records the reason so that unplanned travel can be measured rather than argued about.

Changes and cancellations are made in MosaicOne Travel. Where a trip is cancelled for company reasons, any change fee or non-refundable balance is a
company cost. Where a trip is cancelled for personal reasons and no company need existed, the traveller repays a non-refundable balance above USD 200.

Every trip needs manager approval before booking. Trips involving more than four travellers from the same team, or trips with a total estimated cost
above USD 10,000, additionally require director approval.

Economy is the standard cabin for all air travel. Premium economy is permitted on scheduled flight segments of 6 hours or more, measured segment by
segment rather than across a whole itinerary.

Business class is permitted only for scheduled flight segments of 10 hours or more, and only with vice-president approval obtained before booking. A
documented medical need is accommodated at any segment length through People Operations, and the medical detail is never shared with the manager or the
approver.

Seat selection fees, one checked bag and, on segments over four hours, an extra-legroom seat are reimbursable in economy. Upgrades purchased by the
traveller with personal funds or personal loyalty points are never reimbursed and never require approval.

Travellers keep their own frequent-flyer benefits. Choosing a materially more expensive itinerary to earn status is not permitted; MosaicOne flags a
booking more than USD 150 above the cheapest reasonable option and asks for a one-line reason.

The travel management provider maintains negotiated fares with a small set of carriers on the company's highest-volume routes: Austin–Boston,
Austin–Berlin, Boston–Berlin and Austin–San Jose. Booking a preferred carrier on those routes is expected where the schedule works.

A non-preferred carrier may be booked where it saves more than USD 100, where the preferred carrier's schedule adds more than three hours to the
journey, or where the traveller has a documented safety or accessibility reason.

Mosaic Robotics does not restrict travel to any lawful carrier on safety grounds beyond the provider's own standard exclusions. Travellers with a
personal concern about a specific carrier may choose another at equal or lower cost without giving a reason.

The standard lodging cap is USD 250 per night before taxes and fees. The cap covers the room rate only; local occupancy taxes, resort fees and
mandatory service charges are reimbursable above it.

The cap rises to USD 350 per night in Boston, New York, San Francisco, London, Zurich and Tokyo, and for any city during a period when a conference the
company is attending has inflated local rates. MosaicOne Travel applies the higher cap automatically for those markets.

Where the cap cannot be met — a remote field site with one hotel, a sold-out market — the traveller books the most reasonable available option and
notes the reason. No pre-approval is needed; the note is enough.

In-room charges are reimbursable only for internet access and for meals claimed within the meal cap. Minibar, laundry on trips under five nights, pay
television and spa charges are not.

Employees on trips of more than 14 nights should ask MosaicOne Travel for an extended-stay or serviced-apartment rate, which is usually cheaper than a
hotel and always more comfortable.

Sharing a room is never required and is never a condition of approval.

The order of preference for ground transport is public transit, then a ride-hailing or taxi service, then a rental car. Rental cars are appropriate
where a field site is not reachable by transit, where equipment must be carried, or where multiple sites are visited in one day.

Rental cars are booked in the compact or intermediate class. A larger class is reimbursable where three or more travellers share the vehicle or where
equipment requires the space. Prepaid fuel options are not reimbursable; the traveller refuels before returning the car and claims the fuel.

The collision damage waiver offered by the rental company is reimbursable for international rentals and is not needed for domestic rentals, which are
covered by the company's own policy. Personal accident insurance sold at the rental desk is never reimbursable.

Employees who drive their own vehicle for business are reimbursed at the statutory mileage rate published by the tax authority of the entity that
employs them, claimed against a start and end address rather than an odometer photograph. Commuting between home and the employee's assigned office is
never reimbursable.

Airport parking is reimbursable for trips of up to seven days at the long-stay rate; for longer trips a return ride-hail journey is usually cheaper and
should be preferred.

International business travel requires manager approval before booking and, for destinations outside the approved-country list in the Tax & Location
Addendum, a note to mobility@mosaicrobotics.example so that the trip is visible to the mobility team.

A business trip of 30 consecutive days or fewer does not trigger the Tax & Legal review that the Tax & Location Addendum requires for *working* from
another country, provided the traveller's activity is genuinely travel — meetings, installation, training, a conference — and not the ordinary conduct
of their role from a foreign desk. Where a trip's character is unclear, the mobility team decides, not the traveller.

The device and network requirements in the Security & Acceptable Use Policy apply in full to international travel. IT Security must be notified of the
destination country at least 5 business days before departure, and travellers to countries on the elevated-risk list are issued a loaner laptop.

Passport, visa and entry-permit costs incurred specifically for a business trip are reimbursable, including expedited processing where the timing was

Vaccinations and medications required for a business destination are reimbursable in full. Mosaic Robotics carries a business travel accident and

Travellers may claim actual meal costs against the caps in the Expenses & Reimbursement Policy, or a per diem, but never both on the same day. The

The international per diem is USD 85 per full day of travel. The domestic per diem is USD 60 per full day. A departure or return day is claimed at 75%

Per diem is not paid for a day on which the company provides all meals — a conference with full catering, an offsite with hosted meals. Where one meal

Per diem requires no receipts. It is reported to payroll where the entity's tax rules treat any part of it as income, and MosaicOne handles that
automatically.

Mosaic Robotics, Inc. expects every person who works here to be able to do their best work without
having to absorb behaviour that makes it harder.
This policy states the standard the company holds itself to, describes the conduct that is prohibited,
and explains what happens when someone raises a
concern.
It applies to every employee, officer and director of Mosaic Robotics, Inc. and Mosaic Robotics
GmbH, and to contractors, interns, agency workers and
visitors while they are engaged with the company. It applies at company premises, at customer and
supplier sites, at company events on and off site, in
company systems, and in work-related communication of any kind, including chat, email, video calls
and public channels.
The policy is written to be used. It is short on abstraction and long on process, because a person
deciding whether to raise a concern needs to know
what will happen next far more than they need a statement of values.
Managers carry an additional duty under this policy. A manager who becomes aware of conduct
that may breach it must report it to People Operations,
even where the person affected has asked them not to and even where the manager judges it
minor. That duty is not discretionary, and the manager
fundamentals training covers how to hold that conversation well.

Four expectations describe the standard.
Treat people as colleagues. Disagree with the work, not the person. Assume competence and good
faith until you have real evidence otherwise, and
say so plainly when you do have it.
Be direct and be kind. Directness without kindness is carelessness. Kindness without directness
leaves people to discover problems on their own.
Mosaic Robotics expects both at once, which is harder and worth it.
Respect boundaries. People differ in what they find comfortable, and the standard is set by the
person on the receiving end rather than by the
person speaking. A comment that was well meant can still be unwelcome, and the right response to
being told so is to stop.
Speak up. A concern raised early is nearly always easier to resolve than the same concern raised a
year later. The company would far rather hear a
concern that turns out to be a misunderstanding than fail to hear one that was real.
These expectations are assessed in the performance cycle alongside delivery. An employee who
delivers well and treats colleagues badly is not
performing well, and the performance and compensation process reflects that.

Harassment is unwelcome conduct, based on a protected characteristic or otherwise, that has the
purpose or effect of violating a person's dignity or of
creating an intimidating, hostile, degrading, humiliating or offensive environment.
Harassment can be verbal, written, visual or physical. It can be a single serious act or a pattern of
smaller ones. It does not require intent: conduct
that was intended as humour is harassment if it has that effect and continues after the person has
said so.
Sexual harassment includes unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favours, unwelcome
physical contact, sexual comments about a person's body or
appearance, and the display or circulation of sexual material. It also includes conditioning any
employment benefit on a sexual response.
Bullying is harassment for the purposes of this policy. Persistent criticism directed at a person rather
than their work, deliberate exclusion,
setting someone up to fail, and shouting are all covered, whether or not any protected characteristic
is involved.
Conduct outside working hours that materially affects a colleague's ability to work is within scope.
The company does not police private life, and it
does act where private conduct follows a person into the workplace.

Discrimination is treating a person less favourably because of a protected characteristic, or applying
a rule that disadvantages people with a
protected characteristic without a genuine and proportionate business reason.
Protected characteristics under this policy are race, colour, ethnic or national origin, nationality,
religion or belief, sex, gender identity and
expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, pregnancy and maternity, marital or civil partnership
status, veteran status, and genetic information.
Where local law protects more, local law applies.
Discrimination is prohibited in every employment decision: hiring, assignment, access to training,
promotion, compensation, discipline and separation.
It is equally prohibited in the informal decisions that precede formal ones, such as who is invited to a
meeting where a decision will be made.
Reasonable accommodation for disability, religious observance and pregnancy is not a favour and
is not discretionary. Requests go to People Operations
and are answered within 10 business days.

Retaliation against a person who reports a concern in good faith is prohibited and is itself a violation
of this policy. It is prohibited whether or not
the underlying concern is upheld, provided the report was made in good faith.
Retaliation includes obvious acts such as dismissal, demotion, an unjustified poor rating or the
removal of good work. It also includes the quieter
forms: exclusion from meetings, withdrawal of informal support, a sudden increase in scrutiny, or a
change in tone that a reasonable person would find
punitive.
Retaliation is prohibited against the person who raised the concern, against witnesses, and against
anyone who participates in an investigation. People
Operations checks in with reporters and witnesses at 30, 90 and 180 days after a case closes,
specifically to detect it.
A finding of retaliation is treated at least as seriously as a finding on the original concern, and in
practice more seriously, because retaliation
attacks the mechanism the company relies on to hear about problems at all.

A concern may be raised in four ways. To the employee's direct manager. To the manager's
manager. Directly to People Operations at
people-ops@mosaicrobotics.example. Or, for harassment, discrimination and retaliation specifically,
to Employee Relations at
employee-relations@mosaicrobotics.example.
An anonymous report may be made through the third-party ethics line, whose number and web
address are published in MosaicOne and on the notice board at
each site. Anonymous reports are investigated as far as the information allows, and the company is
honest that anonymity sometimes limits what can be
done.
There is no requirement to raise a concern with the manager first. A person who is uncomfortable
doing so, for any reason or for none, may go straight
to People Operations or Employee Relations.
A report should say what happened, when, where, who was present and what the person would like
to happen. None of those elements is mandatory. A report
that consists only of "something is wrong and I do not know how to describe it" is a valid report and
will be taken seriously.
Concerns about a member of the executive team are handled by the chair of the audit committee
rather than by People Operations, and the ethics line
routes them there automatically.

People Operations acknowledges every reported concern within 2 business days. The
acknowledgement names the person who will handle the case, explains
the process, and sets out what the reporter can expect to be told and when.
Not every concern becomes a formal investigation. Some are resolved by a conversation, some by
a change of arrangement, some by coaching. The reporter
is told which route is proposed and why, and may ask for a formal investigation instead.
Where a formal investigation is opened, an investigator is appointed who has no reporting
relationship to anyone involved. The investigator interviews
the reporter, the person the concern is about, and any witnesses, and reviews any relevant records.
The person the concern is about is told the
substance of the allegation and given a fair opportunity to respond.
Investigations are targeted for completion within 30 calendar days of the report. Where an
investigation will take longer, the reporter and the
respondent are both told, in writing, why and when to expect the outcome.

Policy. Gifts to public officials of any value are
prohibited. An offer that would create an obligation, of any size, is refused and disclosed.
Disclosure resolves nearly every conflict. Failing to disclose one, and being found out later, resolves
nothing and is itself a conduct matter.

Outcomes under this policy range from a documented conversation, through formal coaching, a
written warning, removal of management responsibility and
withholding of a bonus or increase, to dismissal.
The outcome depends on the seriousness of the conduct, its effect on others, whether it was
repeated, whether the person had been told before, and
whether they took responsibility once it was raised. Contribution to the company is not a mitigating
factor and never has been.
Certain conduct results in dismissal in almost every case: physical violence or a credible threat of it,
sexual harassment involving physical contact or
coercion, deliberate falsification of company records, and retaliation against a reporter after a formal
warning about it.
Outcomes are recorded in the employee's file and are visible to People Operations and to the
employee. A warning remains live for 12 months for the
purposes of considering a later matter, and stays on file after that.
Where the respondent is a contractor, agency worker or visitor, the outcome is a change to or the
end of their engagement, arranged with the supplying
firm through Procurement.

Mosaic Robotics does not prohibit alcohol at company events and does expect judgement. An
employee whose
conduct at a company event would breach this policy in the office breaches it at the event, and the
fact
that drink was involved is neither an excuse nor an aggravating factor on its own.
Every company event serves a full non-alcoholic selection, ends at a stated time, and has a named
organiser
who is responsible for the arrangements. Nobody is asked to explain why they are not drinking, and
no
activity at a company event is contingent on drinking.
Being unfit for work through alcohol or drugs is a safety matter as well as a conduct matter, and on
a
manufacturing floor or a customer site it is treated with the seriousness a moving robot deserves. A
manager who believes an employee is unfit removes them from the area, arranges for them to get
home safely,
and contacts People Operations the same day.

Everything raised under this policy is handled on a need-to-know basis. Investigation records are
held in a
restricted store separate from the ordinary employee file, and a manager is never given access to a
case
record about their own team.
Participants in an investigation, including the reporter and the respondent, are asked not to discuss
the
matter outside the process. That request protects everyone: an account that circulates informally is
harder
to test, and a person who is later found to have done nothing wrong cannot un-circulate it.
The company cannot promise a reporter that nothing will happen. Where a matter involves a risk to
another
person, the company must act, and People Operations says so at the outset rather than discovering
the
conflict halfway through.
Records are retained for six years after closure and are then destroyed, unless a legal hold applies.
Aggregate statistics on volume, category and resolution time are reported to the executive team and
the
board quarterly, with no identifying detail and with small categories combined so that nobody can be
inferred from the numbers.
Anyone who discloses case information outside the need-to-know boundary is themselves subject
to this
policy. The confidentiality of the process is what makes the process usable.
